known_facts_book1: A thin, skinny old man with a big fat nose, little eyes set close together, thin white hair and brown skin seared with furrows, who wears spectacles tied on with a ribbon.
Was a common shoemaker in the City of Herku until he found his great-grandfather's books of magical recipes and instruments hidden in his attic.
Is descended from the greatest wizard and sorcerer who ever lived; even his father practiced magic before wandering away from Herku and never coming back.
Once took two teaspoonfuls of zosozo instead of one, and became so strong that leaning against the city wall pushed it over.
Built himself a wicker castle in the hills west of Herku and practiced his ancestors' magic there for a full year before acting.
Learned from his ancestors' books of a jeweled gold dishpan in the Yip Country which would grow large enough to sit in and transport its rider instantly anywhere in Oz.
Stole Cayke's dishpan first, and used it to rob Glinda's castle, the Wizard's rooms and Ozma's apartments all in one night.
Threw a scarf over Ozma's head when she confronted him, tied her fast, and carried her off in the dishpan with the plunder.
Enchanted Ozma into a golden peach pit inside a single tempting peach placed at the exact center of the Great Orchard — and then, being occupied, forgot her.
Does not suspect in the least that he is wicked; his ambition blinds him to the rights of others.
Defends the castle with three barriers, all of them stolen tricks: Glinda's Barrier of Fire, the Wizard's Wall of Steel, and an optical illusion of hundreds of girl-soldiers.
Traps the whole party by tipping the great domed hall until it turns upside down, and watches from a golden cage that stays put.
Is transformed into a dove by Dorothy's Magic Belt, but fights the enchantment hard enough to make the dove enormous — a spiteful Dove of War, not a Dove of Peace.
Escapes by flying into the stolen dishpan and wishing himself to the northeast corner of the Quadling Country.
Comes to Dorothy weeks later in the royal gardens to ask forgiveness, and **refuses** her offer to restore his man's shape, preferring to remain a dove.

known_relations_book1.Ozma: The Ruler he steals and hides in a peach pit.
known_relations_book1.Cayke: The Cookie Cook whose magic dishpan makes his whole plan possible.
known_relations_book1.Dorothy: The girl who transforms him into a dove and later forgives him.
known_relations_book1.the Wizard: Whose black bag and Wall of Steel trick he stole.
known_relations_book1.Glinda: Whose Great Book of Records and chemicals he stole.
known_relations_book1.the Czarover of Herku: The ruler of the city he abandoned, who warns the party against him.
